# The fifth review passed, and three of its findings were worth a round anyway

The fifth review returned no ticket. It re-ran the suite at 1,557 tests, the rule set at
23 of 23 fixtures and the tree clean, read every criterion's evidence, and judged its
seven findings not blocking. Ruud's decision was to fix the three medium ones before
delivering rather than carry them, and the reason the decision was worth taking is that
all three are in the rules this ticket exists to deliver, not in the account of them.
Red 322 and green 323 are the round.

## F22, the deny-list that was mostly dead

`dependency-cruiser/core-no-io` matched its seven IO libraries only as
`node_modules/<lib>/`, where its three sibling deny-lists in the same file all write
`(^|node_modules/)`. A specifier resolves to a `node_modules` path when the package is
installed and to the bare name when it is not, which is the state of every dependency at
the moment somebody writes the import. **None of the seven is installed at this
repository's root**, so the clause was carrying nothing: measured both ways, `import
{ Queue } from 'bullmq'` in `packages/core/src` was accepted before the fix and is
refused after it, by name. The money core's import boundary now reads what its registry
entry says it reads.

Two tests: one compares all four library deny-lists and fails if any of them stops
anchoring the bare specifier, which is the comparison that would have caught this; one
runs dependency-cruiser over a real probe and asserts `core-no-io` names it.

## F24, the shape a fee schedule is actually written in

`ast-grep/money-as-integer-cents` matched a non-integer literal only in a
`variable_declarator`, while its registry entry says it reads such a literal bound to a
name that says it is money. So `const priceEur = 19.99` was refused and
`const schedule = { feeCents: 1.5 }` and `class Tariff { private price = 19.99 }` were
not. SEEN-016 encodes fee schedules per marketplace and SEEN-071 models margin from cost
layers, and a schedule is an object literal and a tariff a class field, so the two shapes
the rule missed are the two the next tickets will write. The rule now carries `pair` and
`public_field_definition` beside the declarator, the node kinds measured rather than read
off the grammar, and the test asserts all four diagnostics the three shapes should
produce. The tree is still clean under the widened rule, which was the thing to check.

## F23, the test CI did not have

`StagedPathWithASpaceTest` is the only test that runs `scripts/rules.sh` rather than
reading it, and it skips where the workspace is absent. The job that runs the harness
suite does not install the workspace and the jobs that install never run the suite, so it
skipped in every job and F21's fix was guarded in CI by two substring assertions over the
script's text. It is now a named step in the job that installs, one second beside a
six-minute suite, and a test asserts the workflow names it.

## The four low findings

F25 is corrected rather than carried, because it was a census and a census is a figure:
three tracked files carry an em dash, not one, the third being `supabase/config.toml`
twice. Both are third-party output, which is the class the paragraph's next clause is
already about, so the whole-tree rule F17 asks for now has its exclusions sized from the
census. F26, F27 and F28 are carried with their reproductions: the credential rule
refusing any base64 JSON, the coverage check declaring no model, and `fixture_results`
going quiet on an entry whose tool has no runner.

## What the next round does

The replay, and this time three production files moved, so nothing earlier can be cited:
`.harness-drafts/replay2.sh` for the five slice pairs, `round6.sh` for the sixth,
`round7.sh` for F21's, and `round8.sh` for this one, which takes the commit before the fix
as its argument. Then the three measurements, the tdd record with every count read out of
its check, the ticket file final **before** the regression, and the regression and the
coverage last with the fingerprint confirmed against the regression.

Twenty-eight findings over five reviews. Twenty-four are closed, four are carried. The
rule set has been re-run independently by three reviewers and holds; what five reviews
have mostly been finding is the account of the work, and what the fifth found instead was
two rules whose entries promised more than their patterns read, which is the most useful
thing any of them has returned.
